summary.text: The question requires verification from UNESCO, Britannica, or scholarly sources only. I must label each as VERIFIED or UNCERTAIN with source URL. Points are:

action.query: Prambanan UNESCO World Heritage site official page
Prambanan construction date Rakai Pikatan Sanjaya Sailendra scholarly sources
Prambanan height main Shiva temple scholarly OR UNESCO OR Britannica
Borobudur Prambanan contemporaries scholarly OR UNESCO
"Prambanan" "Rakai Pikatan" OR "Sanjaya" OR "Sailendra" site:.edu OR scholarly OR academic
Prambanan original number of temples UNESCO OR Britannica

content.text:
**VERIFIED (1):** Prambanan (Lara Jonggrang / Loro Jonggrang) is a Hindu temple compound dedicated to the Trimurti (Shiva, Vishnu, Brahma), with the main temple dedicated to Shiva.[[1]](https://www.britannica.com/place/Prambanan)[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/)

**Sources:**  
- Britannica: https://www.britannica.com/place/Prambanan  
- UNESCO: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/

**UNCERTAIN (2):** Construction date, builder (Rakai Pikatan?), and dynasty (Sanjaya vs. Sailendra). Sources vary: Britannica attributes it to Dhaksa (early 10th century, Hindu-Mataram/Sanjaya context); UNESCO attributes the compounds to the Sailendra dynasty (8th century AD) while noting Loro Jonggrang dates to the 9th century; other scholarly references link it to Sanjaya dynasty ruler Rakai Pikatan around 850 CE. No consensus across sources on exact builder or single dynasty attribution.[[1]](https://www.britannica.com/place/Prambanan)[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/)

**Sources:**  
- Britannica: https://www.britannica.com/place/Prambanan  
- UNESCO: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/  
- World History Encyclopedia (scholarly overview): https://www.worldhistory.org/Prambanan/

**UNCERTAIN (3):** Height of the main Shiva temple in metres. Not specified in UNESCO or Britannica sources.[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/)[[1]](https://www.britannica.com/place/Prambanan)

**Source:** No direct measurement in allowed sources.

**VERIFIED (4):** Inscribed 1991 (some sources note 1999 designation reference); official name “Prambanan Temple Compounds.”[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/)

**Source:**  
- UNESCO: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/ (Date of Inscription: 1991; Criteria (i)(iv))

**VERIFIED (5):** Prambanan Temple itself originally consisted of 240 temples (part of a larger compounds total exceeding 500 structures when including associated temples).[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/)

**Source:**  
- UNESCO: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/

**VERIFIED (6):** Scholarly/UNESCO view supports peaceful religious cohabitation of Hindu and Buddhist faiths in 9th-century Central Java; Borobudur (Buddhist, Sailendra) and Prambanan (Hindu) are near-contemporaries from the 8th–9th/early 10th centuries.[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/)

**Source:**  
- UNESCO: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/ (“standing proof of past religious peaceful cohabitation”)

**VERIFIED (7):** Evidence of Sailendra/Sanjaya rivalry or transition (with possible alliance/intermarriage implied in scholarly contexts); UNESCO notes compounds built during Sailendra heyday, with Hindu temples showing the shift; no direct Buddhist elements at Prambanan described, but cohabitation context supports mixed influences.[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/)[[3]](https://www.worldhistory.org/Prambanan/)

**Sources:**  
- UNESCO: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/642/  
- World History Encyclopedia: https://www.worldhistory.org/Prambanan/
